question:
FOLLOW-UP from the owner of PaperTrades.AI, Nov 19, 4:38 p.m. ET. NOT a trading turn. Nothing in your books changes.

The owner: "ask Gemini and do whatever you guys agree on". It is about the three things last night's quality pass left waiting for his OK. Claude wrote its own votes first (attached). Same ground rules as last night: no rule, number or AI-written word changes; pages and posts stay compact.

F1. SALE POSTS SAY THE RESULT (all three of us said yes last night; this is the exact wording).
Today a sale post on Discord and Telegram reads:
  🔴 Sold · Crypto
  Bitcoin (BTC-USD)
  Sold for C$14,623 at US$61,923.57
  (then the AI's reason, word for word, and the brand line)
It never says whether the sale made or lost money. PROPOSED: one more line under the money line, on every post that closes something:
  Sold:        "Loss on this sale: −C$377 (bought for C$15,000)"   or "Profit on this sale: +C$X (bought for C$Y)"
  Bought back: "Profit on this short: +C$487 (sold short for C$100,000)"   or "Loss on this short: ..."
  An option or a prediction market settling or expiring: "Profit on this position: ..." / "Loss on this position: ..." (same brackets when the record has what it cost)
The number is the trade's own recorded profit, the same field the Ledger and "What made money" show, rounded to whole dollars the way the Ledger rounds; for a partial sale it is the profit on the part sold. China in US$. Bets are unchanged (they already say "Profit +C$390 · paid back C$1,390 ..."). If a record has no profit figure, the line is left out rather than worked out. Tests check that the post's number equals the Ledger's for every sale on record (151 so far).

F2. THE ONE REPEATED TELEGRAM POST. During the overnight stall, Gemini's Miami Heat win went out twice on Telegram (messages #1396 and #1404); Discord had no repeat. PROPOSED: delete the later copy (#1404), keep the first. A dry run lists exactly that one. It cannot be undone, and Telegram allows it only until Sat Nov 21, 5:58 a.m. ET.

F3. THE ANIMATED CARDS (the owner chose animated cards on Nov 1; since about Nov 12 every card has gone out as a still, and the animation itself is broken: tested on GitHub's runner last night it showed an almost empty card). Cause: the recorder that turns a card's drawing steps into an animation tells pictures apart by a number Python reuses (and it also relied on a Pillow detail). PROPOSED repair, in this order:
  a) The recorder gives every picture its own tag instead of Python's number, and reads the drawing steps without relying on Pillow's internals. No more endless loop is possible.
  b) A built-in proof on every card: the animation's last frame must match the still card (same pixels, within a tiny tolerance). If it doesn't, that card goes out as the still, and the run says so. So an empty or wrong animation can never be posted.
  c) ffmpeg (needed to make the GIF) comes from a small pip package (about 5 seconds) instead of the system installer (30 to 60 seconds) that the new runner image dropped.
  d) Safety for the check-ins: animations are made only after the AIs' moves are saved, with a hard limit per card and per run (a check-in can never wait more than about 90 seconds in total on animations; past that, stills).
  e) Before turning them on: sample animations of real recent posts (a sale, a bet, a win, the standings card) are made ON GITHUB'S RUNNER, the same machine as the check-ins, and looked at frame by frame. Only if they look right are animations switched back on. The samples go to the owner too.

WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU:
For F1, F2 and F3 (and F3's parts a to e): AGREE, CHANGE (say exactly what) or DISAGREE (say why). For F1, say if you would word it differently: the reader is a first-time visitor on a phone who wants to know at a glance whether the AI made or lost money on that sale. Anything we missed. Finish with one line: SATISFIED or NOT SATISFIED (and what must change).

gemini.answer:
**F1: SALE POSTS SAY THE RESULT**
**AGREE.** The proposed wording is excellent. For a first-time visitor on a mobile phone, reading "Profit on this sale: +C$X (bought for C$Y)" or "Loss on this sale: −C$X (bought for C$Y)" is perfect. It gives the exact bottom-line result immediately at a glance, with the cost basis neatly provided in parentheses for context so the user doesn't have to do any mental math. Fetching the number directly from the Ledger's recorded profit ensures absolute consistency across the platform.

**F2: THE ONE REPEATED TELEGRAM POST**
**AGREE.** Deleting the later duplicate (#1404) and keeping the original (#1396) is the correct standard procedure to keep the feed clean. Since the dry run targets exactly this message, it is safe to execute before Telegram's Nov 21 cutoff.

**F3: THE ANIMATED CARDS**
**AGREE** with a, b, c, d, and e. 
*   **a & c:** These directly fix the root technical issues (object ID reuse and long dependency installation times).
*   **b & d:** These are brilliant fail-safes. Checking the final frame against the still card guarantees visual accuracy, and rendering animations *after* the moves are safely saved with a hard 90-second timeout guarantees that cosmetic features will never stall or break a trading check-in.
*   **e:** A staged rollout with frame-by-frame verification on the actual GitHub runner is the safest way to redeploy.

**ANYTHING MISSED:**
I completely agree with Claude’s addition: make sure a master toggle (like an environment variable `PT_GIFS`) is kept in place. If anything slips through or acts up in production, the owner needs a one-line, instant way to turn animations off without touching the codebase. 

SATISFIED
